spine.active_goal: Author two standalone SPECs: SPEC A for config staging/live promotion, then SPEC B for mitosis cost, codegen decomposition and stacked PRs. Neither inherits the 2026-07-30 document.
spine.next_step: Fresh session: resume superpowers:brainstorming at step 4 (propose approaches) for SPEC A ONLY. Read this thread's 2026-08-06T19-31 session event FIRST - it holds the engine map, stacked-PR research and config inventory; do NOT re-derive them. spine.last_session: Ran brainstorming steps 1-4: settled scope as two SPECs, settled the merge model, and refuted dynamic import in the Workflow runtime by direct measurement. No SPEC drafted.

open_risks.text: Instrument per-dispatch context before trusting any collapse win — the 2026-07-30 plan counts dispatches and wall-clock only, so Decompose fusion, Ship 13-to-1, and per-MSP reviews would all score as wins even if cost rose.

Re-derive every line citation from the current tree — mitosis.js is 5,515 lines against the cited 4,851, the phase-parity gate appears already landed, and mitosis-git.mjs moved to .claude/lib/git/pr.mjs.
Decide telemetry before making any cost claim — no token or tool-call accounting exists anywhere in the engine, so every re-exploration claim is unmeasurable today.

Do not re-run the three investigations — the engine map, stacked-PR research and config inventory cost roughly 340k subagent tokens, their transcripts do not survive, and the 2026-08-06T19-31 session event is the only remaining copy.

Telemetry must count tokens, not dispatches — no token or tool-call accounting exists in the engine today, and a dispatch-only instrument would score a phase collapse as a win even if token cost rose.
settings.json is a two-way surface — Claude Code writes it itself via permission prompts, model selection and plugin toggles, so a one-way staging-to-live promotion would silently clobber live edits.
Live settings.json has already diverged from the tracked copy — live permissions are broader than the repo's, so the repo does not currently describe what is actually enforced.
parallel-plan-execution.js is dead code — its top-level dynamic imports cannot execute in the Workflow runtime, so any design routing work through it builds on a broken entry point.

Re-derive every line citation from the current tree — mitosis.js is 5,515 lines against the 2026-07-30 document's cited 4,851, phase parity appears landed, and mitosis-git.mjs moved to .claude/lib/git/pr.mjs.

key_decisions.title: Dependent MSP chains merge with merge-commit; standalone PRs keep squash
Workflow runtime forbids dynamic import, so codegen is the only path off the twinning tax
Split the re-spec into two specs, config promotion landing before the mitosis core

out_of_scope: Implementing any MSP from either SPEC
Editing mitosis.js, the parallel engine, or any live config path while a SPEC is being authored
